key_insight: Large language models show exploit–explore-like semantic search dynamics: they cluster related concepts and switch categories when internal activations signal depleted category evidence.
engineering_relevance: Mechanistic interpretability can reveal and steer internal search states in LLMs, suggesting new controls for generation behavior, probing, and safety alignment.
method: Applied the Jacobian lens (J-lens) to map residual-stream states to token-level activations.
Tracked concept/category activations during semantic fluency generation to detect exploit vs. explore transitions.
Derived steering vectors and generic residual directions to causally bias category switching rates.
evidence_signal: Across semantic fluency-style generation, switching was associated with low next-token activations and category-specific J-lens depletion, with steering experiments used to validate causality.
watch_item: The findings are based on specific tasks and interpretability probes, so transferability of the steering directions to other prompts, models, or generation settings may be limited.
paper_title: Signatures of semantic search in the activations of large language models
